From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Residency certainty & snapshot strategy — follow-up and next steps

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery call and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the technical deep dive: 

- High-level ask we took away: EU-residency for EU tenant data (both prompt payloads and derived embeddings), scoped retention for logs, and ability to fail over to a separate region for DR while keeping primary data in-region.
- PII handling: you emphasized that HealthGrid considers patient identifiers PHI-equivalent and wants them to not persist beyond inference unless explicitly stored by you.
- Retention targets: your team suggested session logs retained no longer than 30 days, with audit logs (access and admin events) retained 12 months for compliance.
- Failover model: prefer warm standby in EU but acceptable to have cold cross-region backups in US for disaster recovery with documented RTO/RPO.

Can you confirm the following so our technical team can prepare concrete options: 
1) Which subset of datasets must be guaranteed EU-only (prompts, embeddings, inference cache, backups)?
2) Maximum acceptable RPO (minutes/hours) and RTO for the failover scenario.
3) Any specific KMS/HSM requirements for key residency or rotation policies.

I attached a short matrix (residency-playbook.xlsx) that maps the common data artifacts we usually see to residency/retention options — if you can mark the columns you care about it will speed the review.

Suggested next steps: technical deep dive with Ben Carter (security) and Marissa Cole (solutions) — are you available Thu 3/29 or Fri 3/30 in the morning?

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

[hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com]

Thanks, Hannah — great summary. Quick answers inline: 

- EU-only: prompts and embeddings for EU customers must remain in EU at rest and in transit. We are OK with ephemeral KV/cache being out-of-region if it does not persist beyond inference (max 1 hour).
- RPO/RTO: target RPO = 1 hour, preferred RTO = 4 hours for a partial region outage. If it's significantly more expensive to meet those numbers we can discuss tiering by workload.
- KMS: we use a cloud KMS but need customer-managed keys (CMK) for production EU tenants; rotation policies are quarterly.

We confirmed internal stakeholders: Paul Morris (Infra) and Alicia (Legal) should review the residency matrix as well — looping Paul into the next thread. 

I can do Thu 3/29 morning ET (that should be 8am PT) for the technical deep dive.

Best,
Emily

Hi all —

A few operational clarifications from my side based on Emily's constraints and the RPO/RTO targets: 

- Snapshot cadence: to meet RPO=1 hour we need hourly incremental snapshots of the minimal persistence layer (embeddings + persisted artifacts). Full daily snapshots are recommended for long-term backups. 
- Encryption & KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) for regionally-held keys. For EU-only residency we can keep the CMK in the EU region and perform encryption/decryption there; cross-region snapshot copies will remain encrypted and only restorable with the CMK if you allow key replicas.
- Cross-region copies: we can keep cold snapshot copies in a US bucket encrypted with your CMK replica; those copies can be configured with a retention TTL (we normally set 90 days for DR copies unless compliance requires otherwise).
- Logging: access logs (admin, infra) will be stored for 12 months in the EU project. Application-level session logs that contain PII will be truncated & redacted before being written to persistent storage; ephemeral traces used for inference optimization are bounded to 1 hour and then wiped.

Action items: 
1) HealthGrid: confirm acceptance of hourly incremental snapshots for RPO=1h and TTL on cross-region copies (proposed 90 days).
2) HealthGrid: confirm CMK rotation window (you mentioned quarterly) and whether you plan to restrict key replication outside EU.
3) Redwood: we'll draft the one-page options doc and attach estimated incremental cost delta for hourly snapshots + cross-region cold storage. Expect the doc in advance of Thu's call.

If we agree these are reasonable tradeoffs we can proceed with the deep dive and a short PILOT statement of work that captures the restore runbook and monitoring hooks.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
